title: TiLiA file (.tla), format 1.0.0-draft.1
description: The layout decided in TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161 (WP3, FR-005). A reader that doesn't use tilia-core fills in the defaults below itself. It checks a file's structure: required keys, types and id formats. Keys it doesn't know are allowed, since the core keeps them (FR-051a). Three things JSON Schema can't check are the core's alone: that each id is used once (a row's, in its timeline), that each reference names something that exists, and that no object has the same key twice. Every other limit, such as a minimum or a list of values, is described, not enforced: the core reads a value that breaks one, and its rules warn where they apply; so are the rules the core only warns about, such as the syntax of `vocabulary` (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#306). A null is a missing key: it is allowed on every key that isn't required, and means the key's default. Attributes of a known kind are left out of the file when they equal their default (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161, point 6); the defaults are the `default` of each property. A default that depends on another value is the extra annotation `x-default-from`, which names that value; such a key is written whenever it is set and left out when it isn't, never compared with the value it would derive (desktop#700). This file is the one place the defaults are kept: the core reads them from here.

version.description: The format version (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#7). Before the freeze, 1.0.0-draft.N (Q2).

time_unit.description: The unit of every time in the file (T12): "seconds" or "quarters".

path.description: Relative to the file's folder, with /; absolute only when no relative path exists; a URL as it is; empty without media (FR-033).

timelines.description: Keyed by id, written in id order (research R7).

scores.description: Empty for a file without a score (FR-130); written in id order.

id.description: A UUID in lower-case hex (UUIDv7 for timelines and components, FR-004).

time.description: In the file's time unit; never rounded (T5).

metadata.description: Named values, each a text or a list of texts (FR-070), in the order they were added (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161, point 1). Recognised: role, author (one full name), source, vocabulary (id@version or a bare id; checked with a warning, not here) on timelines; tags (a list) and generated_by on components and measures. Left out of a timeline, component or measure when empty.

components.description: Keyed by id, written in id order.

height.description: From 0. Always written where a kind has one: TiLiA's default height comes from each user's settings, so it can't be a default of the format.

measure_table.description: The id of the beat timeline whose measures place this timeline: a score timeline's, or that of a timeline imported by measure (FR-086, FR-133).

timeline.description: A timeline of a known kind is checked against that kind, spelled as the writer writes it; one of a kind the core doesn't know is kept as it is (FR-015), with only its kind, name, ordinal and metadata checked, as every timeline's are, since the core uses them (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#313).

components.description: None: a slider has none, and an AudioWave timeline's are built from the media and not stored (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161, point 9).

beat_pattern.description: TiLiA's rule for making new measures, as text (desktop#621's syntax, such as "10[4] 3").

show_time_signatures.description: Display setting (desktop#621). Migrated files from before time signatures have false.

measure_source.description: Where the measures came from (T12, Q9); a measure's own `source` overrides it.

then.description: A harmony timeline has no height of its own; its levels have one.

rows.description: In display order, top to bottom (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161, point 14).

id.description: Six letters and digits, unique in its timeline; kept as stored.

score.description: The id of an entry of `scores` (FR-133); left out before a score is imported.

measure_source.description: Where values came from (T12): tapped (made by a person in TiLiA), score, import, unknown (converted by the migration, Q9), or edited (from a score, an import or the migration, then changed by a person; TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161).

measure.description: On a beat that starts a measure; the first beat always has one (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161). A measure's beats are the beats from its mark to the next one. Always written, even empty (`{}`): its presence marks the downbeat, so it is never left out as a default.

number.description: The printed bar number, written whenever it is set: a pickup's 0, a repeat going back, an ending or a cadenza sharing a number, a restart. Without one, a measure is the previous measure's number plus one, and the first measure is 1 (desktop#700).

label.description: The printed name, when it isn't the number ("16a", "2c").

cadenza.description: A cadenza: it has no pass, and doesn't count towards the passes of its number (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#191).

restart.description: The first bar of a new movement or song in the same file: every pass count starts again here (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#191).

next.description: In a folded table, the measures played after this one, one per pass, by their downbeats' ids (the Measure Map's `next`). Left out when the next measure in the timeline follows.

beat_unit.description: On a beat where the unit changes, applying from the start of that beat's measure (desktop#621). Two in one measure are allowed: TiLiA warns before saving and shows the measure red (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#161, point 10).

units.description: Units per tap, such as "1", "3", "1/2" or "2+3" (desktop#621's syntax; checked with a warning, not here).

component.description: A component of a known kind is checked against that kind; one of a kind the core doesn't know is kept as it is. So is one of a kind its timeline doesn't hold, such as a range in a marker timeline, with a warning: it is checked against its kind here, but the core doesn't follow its references.

row_id.description: The id of one of the timeline's rows.

then.description: Only in a score timeline whose score is a legacy SVG (FR-022): kept from the old file with every attribute TiLiA stored.

format.description: "mei" or "svg-osmd-legacy"; a score of another format is kept as it is.

content.description: The score's lines: CRLF, or any run of CRs before an LF, turned into LF, split on LF, with a final empty element when it ends with a newline; not normalised to NFC (FR-132). Splitting gives at least one line: empty content is [""].

source.description: Where the score came from (FR-131): the original file, its origin, and the converter with its version when it was converted.

license.description: The licence the original file states, as written, never empty, or NOASSERTION until it's filled in (FR-131, TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#171). Left out at NOASSERTION, its default, like any key at its default: a missing key means its default (TimeLineAnnotator/project-management#227).

then.description: A score the migration made from an old file's SVG (FR-022). TiLiA never recorded a source or licence for it. SVG scores are to be deprecated.

beat_x.description: The old viewer's beat positions (viewer_beat_x), as [position, x] pairs in the order of their positions. A position is a place in the score, not a time: the measure number plus the fraction of the measure. x is the beat's x coordinate in the SVG.
